entries.title: North Korean anthem played for South Korea at Asian Games
entries.snippet: Organisers have apologised for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team at the Asian Games in Japan.

entries.title: Dozens of suspected illegal miners die in Nigerian custody
entries.snippet: Authorities linked the deaths to disease, but this has been disputed by intelligence reports and relatives of the accused.

entries.title: Ronaldo named in first Portugal squad since World Cup - at age of 41
entries.snippet: Cristiano Ronaldo is named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus for their upcoming Nations League games.

entries.snippet: The gunman is among the dead in what is the third school shooting in the country since June.

entries.snippet: Since taking control in 1965, Buffett grew a struggling textile mill into a global conglomerate.

entries.snippet: Increasingly frequent and ferocious attacks on the Ukrainian capital have left many on edge.

entries.title: Opinion: Remembering Annie Dillard, nature writer
entries.snippet: With her 1974 book, "Pilgrim at Tinker Creek," Annie Dillard became the youngest woman to win the Pulitzer Prize. We take a moment to remember her and her work.

entries.title: Ancient teeth pose a mystery: What made those strange grooves?
entries.snippet: New research on ancient human remains suggests the habitual usage of betel nuts, a plant seed with mind-affecting properties that is popular in parts of Asia despite the health risks it presents.

entries.title: An Alaska storm scattered artifacts. Archaeologists are racing to save what's left
entries.snippet: Last year, remnants of a typhoon damaged homes, infrastructure and an archaeological dig site. Now, archaeologists are trying to get as many objects out as possible before the next storm.

entries.title: Ever wonder how the Fed's interest rate actually works? We've got answers
entries.snippet: The Federal Reserve just raised interest rates this week for the first time this year. So how does it actually work? And what does it mean for the economy — and the rest of us? Here are some answers.

entries.title: Russia holds parliamentary vote in areas it seized from Ukraine in the war
entries.snippet: Russia's parliamentary election for the first time is being held in Ukraine's regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the start of its full-scale invasion more than 4 1/2 years ago.

entries.title: As Europe warms, Italy sees West Nile virus spread
entries.snippet: Italian health authorities see evidence that rising temperatures and longer warm seasons are helping mosquitoes spread West Nile virus across a wider area, during more months of the year.

entries.title: U.S. and Denmark reach deal to build U.S. military presence in Greenland
entries.snippet: President Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.

entries.title: Alaska's salmon-feasting bears face off in biggest Fat Bear Week ever
entries.snippet: This year's single-elimination tournament will see 16 competitors face off, compared to 12 in past years. Officials report more cubs in Katmai National Park than they've seen in recent memory.

entries.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
entries.snippet: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

entries.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
entries.snippet: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.

entries.title: Trump administration begins building border wall in Big Bend region of Texas
entries.snippet: The start of construction marks an important milestone in the administration's $46 billion plan to line the border with walls, barriers, roads and technology as it seeks to make good on a key campaign promise by Trump to finish the wall.

entries.title: What's in the Greenland agreement between U.S. and Denmark
entries.snippet: On Friday, President Trump declared a deal has been struck with Denmark over its oversight of Greenland. Trump has long coveted the mineral-rich island, which Denmark has controlled since the 1700s. Nick Schifrin reports.

entries.title: Trump says he's banning 3 outlets from White House in his latest attack on press freedom
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump says he is banning three major news outlets, CNN, MS NOW and Politico, from the White House due to what he called "unfavorable coverage." Trump didn't provide details on how the ban would be implemented, but warned he might bar other media outlets as well.

entries.title: Meet Earth's newest wild cat species, living in Bolivia and the first named in over a century
entries.snippet: A previously unknown cat species has been identified in plain sight: at a wildlife sanctuary in Bolivia, where the small, spotted feline had been living for years after being taken in by a local family.

entries.title: U.S.-Saudi nuclear power deal faces pushback over potential weapons risks

entries.title: 'An unworldly experience.' Why scientists flew into firestorm clouds this wildfire season
entries.snippet: As wildfires grow bigger and hotter in many parts of the world, researchers have embarked on an airborne mission to learn more about the severe storm clouds that sometimes form over the most intense blazes.

entries.title: DHS may have violated state election law, Virginia's AG says after whistleblower report
entries.snippet: Virginia's attorney general said Thursday that the Department of Homeland Security may have violated several state laws after a whistleblower accused its employees of misrepresenting themselves on voter lookup tools to hunt for noncitizen voters.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump says he is banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump said Friday that he was banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House due to what he called unfavorable coverage, and threatened that more such media prohibitions could be coming.

entries.title: Judge isn't swayed by government's claims that plans for an 'anti-weaponization fund' are dead
entries.snippet: U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema in Virginia rejected the notion that the case's claims are moot because the Trump administration says the fund is dead and won't go forward.

entries.title: Pentagon moves forward with mandatory testosterone testing for most male troops
entries.snippet: The Pentagon has rolled out formal guidance for mandatory testosterone testing for male service members 30 and older, a policy that leaves out women for now and faces questions from medical experts about the need and efficacy of such a program.

entries.title: Holdout juror in Clancy trial says he didn't have 'any doubts' that she was responsible for killing her kids
entries.snippet: The lone juror who wanted to convict Lindsay Clancy of murder for killing her three children said he was certain of her guilt, but that other jurors wouldn't listen to him, according to a statement released by his lawyer Friday in his first public comments on the case.

entries.title: Attorney General Blanche blurs Justice Department boundaries by appearing at political events
entries.snippet: Attorney General Todd Blanche is blurring traditional boundaries between politics and federal law enforcement with recent speeches at political events that mark a sharp departure from norms meant to protect the Justice Department from the appearance of partisan bias.

entries.title: Early voting begins in U.S. midterm elections that could flip control of Congress
entries.snippet: In-person voting for this year's midterm elections began Friday, ushering in the final six weeks for Americans to decide which party they trust to lead Congress through a cost-of-living crisis, a prolonged war in Iran and other pressing issues.

entries.title: WATCH: Vance brands Democrats as 'lunatics' at rally in Iowa
entries.snippet: Vice President JD Vance on Friday mounted a vigorous defense of the Trump administration's policies and Iowa GOP candidates on the November ballot.

entries.title: Bipartisan criticism from senators about Pentagon briefing on U.S. defense strategy
entries.snippet: Tensions are mounting between the Pentagon and Congress over the flow of information to lawmakers about the U.S. military's priorities, with both Democrats and Republicans accusing a Defense Department leader of being frustratingly opaque.

entries.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
entries.snippet: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

entries.title: Ed Sheeran continues US tour amid Palestinian controversy
entries.snippet: Pro-Palestinian protests are expected at Ed Sheeran's first gig since Macklemore was dropped from the tour. The US rapper shouted "Free Palestine" at a concert in New Jersey.

entries.title: Oktoberfest opens as Munich mayor taps first beer keg
entries.snippet: Thousands of visitors streamed onto Munich's Oktoberfest grounds as the world-famous beer festival got underway. Some spent the night outside the gates to secure coveted places in the festival tents.

entries.title: US court rejects Trump policy on third-country deportations
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has deported more than 25,000 people to countries other than their own. Now a federal appeals court has put the brakes on the policy.

entries.title: India news: British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal granted bail after 9 years in detention
entries.snippet: Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been granted bail after more than eight years without conviction. Meanwhile, India swapped its male flagbearer for the Asian Games opening ceremony over a missing kit. DW has more.

entries.title: Russia votes for new parliament in controlled elections
entries.snippet: Russia is holding its first State Duma election since invading Ukraine, with voting also imposed in occupied Ukrainian regions. President Vladimir Putin's party is expected to dominate the tightly controlled contest.

entries.title: Germany news: Campaigns wrap up in two state elections
entries.snippet: Parties are campaigning for a last day ahead of polls in Mecklenburg-Vorpomerania and Berlin. And an association responsible for German sea ports says they are at high risk from cyberattacks and sabotage. DW has more.

entries.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: SPD seeks to fend off AfD
entries.snippet: For nearly three decades, the Social Democrats have governed Germany's northeastern state. If they can fend off the AfD, the result may boost the fortunes of the German government's junior coalition partner.

entries.title: Pakistan: Suicide bombing death toll rises to at least 31
entries.snippet: More than 100 others have been injured in the militant attack on a police headquarters near the border with Afghanistan. Several militants were still clashing with Pakistan's security forces on Saturday.

entries.title: Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
entries.snippet: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

entries.title: Cuba faces another nationwide blackout amid US fuel blockade
entries.snippet: Millions were left without electricity as Cuba's aging power grid collapsed under the weight of fuel shortages, deteriorating infrastructure and US sanctions.

entries.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked 3 companies during testing
entries.snippet: During a test of its cybersecurity capabilities, Google's Gemini AI model accessed the internet and hacked other companies. This is the first known instance of Google's AI systems engaging in such behavior autonomously.

entries.title: Trump signs broad Russia sanctions bill
entries.snippet: The bill signed by US President Donald Trump targets officials, banks, and a fleet of shadow tankers that transport Russian energy.

entries.title: US, Denmark reach deal over Greenland's security, Trump says
entries.snippet: The deal with Denmark, according to President Donald Trump, would give the US "permanent control" over Greenland's security. Denmark said the deal is "great for NATO and Europe."

entries.title: Trump bars CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump has accused CNN, MS NOW and Politico of spreading fake news. The outlets have vowed to take legal action against the ban.

entries.title: Iran's 'new Hezbollah:' How powerful are the Houthis now?
entries.snippet: After Houthi victories in Yemen, the group's importance in the US-Iran war has grown. Previously Lebanon's Hezbollah was considered most significant in Iran's "axis of resistance." Now the Houthis are rising to the top.

entries.title: Ryanair boss apologizes for calling other airlines 'rapists'
entries.snippet: The airline CEO had used the term to describe other airlines with high fares. His comments were criticized by officials both in Ireland and the UK.

entries.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
entries.snippet: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.
